title: Derived geometric-point direct image is global sections with its adjunction
statement:
Let $\Omega$ be an algebraically closed field, $s=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, $Z$ any scheme and $h:Z\to s$ a morphism. Let $S_D:D(s_{\mathrm{Et}},\mathbf Z)\to D(\mathbf Z)$ and $C_s$ be the termwise geometric-stalk and constant-complex functors of [lem-kun-geometric-point-derived-constants]. Write $C_Z$ for the constant-complex functor [def-kun-constant-sheaf], $h^{-1}\dashv Rh_*$ for the derived inverse/direct-image adjunction [def-kun-projection-formula-map], and $R\Gamma_Z=R\Gamma(Z_{\mathrm{Et}},-)$ for derived global sections [def-kun-rgamma-unbounded]. Let $\gamma:h^{-1}C_s\xrightarrow{\sim}C_Z$ be the canonical pullback-of-constants comparison [lem-kun-pullback-constant]. There is a natural isomorphism
$$\beta_E:S_D Rh_*E\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_ZE$$
for every $E\in D(Z_{\mathrm{Et}},\mathbf Z)$. It is the isomorphism of right adjoints obtained by identifying the left adjoints $h^{-1}C_s$ and $C_Z$ through $\gamma$. More explicitly, let $\epsilon^s:C_sS_D\to\mathrm{id}$ be the counit of the constant/stalk equivalence, $\epsilon^h:h^{-1}Rh_*\to\mathrm{id}$ the derived direct-image counit, and $\epsilon^Z:C_ZR\Gamma_Z\to\mathrm{id}$ the constant-section counit [def-kun-constant-projection-morphism]. Then, naturally in $E$,
$$\epsilon^Z_E\circ C_Z(\beta_E)\circ\gamma_{S_D Rh_*E}
=\epsilon^h_E\circ h^{-1}(\epsilon^s_{Rh_*E}).$$
For a sheaf $G$ in degree zero, $\beta_G$ on degree-zero cohomology is the canonical identification $S(h_*G)\cong(h_*G)(s)=G(Z)$, induced by inverse to the global-section-to-germ map on $s$. No properness, torsion or finiteness assumption is made.

proof.text: Apply the counit characterization of the unique right-adjoint comparison to the transported composite adjunction. Expand the transported and composite counits and cancel the constants isomorphism. This is a formal categorical calculation and proves the first clause on every unbounded derived object. The named generic canonical comparison and its proved counit API specialize to the original composite.

proof.text: For an arbitrary point of a site with a terminal object, evaluate the constant-section counit after the sheafification unit. Comparison with the constant/evaluation adjunction identifies this evaluation with the section-evaluation comparison. If the constant/point adjunction unit is the canonical germ, its right-adjoint uniqueness comparison is the global-section-to-germ map: expand its unit/counit formula and apply naturality of the map into the point colimit. Specialize to the identity geometric point of Spec Ω, using the fixed unit normalization of the geometric-point constants data.

source.place: Tag 07A6; for the augmentation, derived.tex Tag 05TD.

proof.text: Apply the ordinary sections-adjunction comparison to the section/evaluation adjunctions on Spec Ω and Z and the inverse/direct-image adjunction. Its left-adjoint uniqueness is exactly upperStarConstantSheafIso. Therefore the germ map followed by the ordinary right-adjoint comparison is lowerStarCompGlobalSectionsIso, including its canonical direction.

source.place: Tag 07A6; for the augmentation, derived.tex Tag 05TD.

proof.text: Compute each canonical derived counit on a single-object augmentation by the derived counit factorization and exact-left identification. For the exact stalk adjunction also transport the right-derived functor to its termwise functor. The single-adjunction comparison applied to these normalized counits says that the composite augmentation followed by β equals the single of the ordinary comparison followed by the global-sections augmentation.

source.place: Tag 07A6; for the augmentation, derived.tex Tag 05TD.

proof.text: Apply zeroth homology to the preceding equality. The single right-derived unit normalization identifies both augmentation maps with inverses to the canonical H⁰ comparisons, also after applying the exact stalk. Enough injectives for the sheaf category supplies the usual injective-resolution model, and right-adjointness supplies left exactness. Cancel the augmentation isomorphisms and use naturality of singleFunctorCompHomologyFunctorIso to identify the transported H⁰(β) with the ordinary comparison. Precompose by the germ map and apply Step 3.
